$comment: Registry of every provisioning value the rich-capability work needs.
Sentinel format is __PROVISION_<KEY>__ : greppable, obviously fake, and never a valid value
for the API that consumes it. Code MUST treat an unreplaced sentinel as NOT_CONFIGURED and
return false from its capability flag - never render a working-looking button. A placeholder
that silently no-ops is the exact bug class this family spent a pass removing (shareText).

values.where: Apple Developer portal > Identifiers > Merchant IDs
values.note: The payment processing certificate CSR is generated by the PSP, not by you. Generating the keypair yourself means the PSP can never decrypt a payment.

values.where: your PSP (e.g. 'stripe'); literal 'example' works in TEST environment
values.note: 'example' + TEST env is a fully working sandbox, so this one is testable before provisioning.

values.where: Play Console > Play Games Services > Configuration
values.note: OAuth consent scopes MUST include games, games_lite AND drive.appdata. Omit the third and saved games fails at runtime only.

values.where: Play Console > Credentials, bound to the RELEASE SHA-1
values.note: With Play App Signing the SHA-1 that matters is Google's re-signed cert, NOT your upload key. Wrong one works in debug and fails for every real install.

values.where: Play Console > Credentials, bound to the DEBUG SHA-1
Apple Developer portal > Identifiers > Services IDs
values.blocks: Sign in with Apple ON ANDROID only (iOS uses the App ID capability)
values.note: Apple forces response_mode=form_post when scope is requested, so the redirect URI must be a SERVER that bounces to an app link. There is no client-only path on Android.

values.where: Apple Developer portal > Keys (the .p8 is downloadable ONCE)
values.blocks: Sign in with Apple server-side token exchange
values.note: Client secret is a JWT that EXPIRES every 6 months. A rotation job is mandatory, not optional.

values.blocks: Sign in with Apple, Apple Pay, all signed builds

neverInRepo: any OAuth client SECRET (as opposed to client ID)
secretsPolicy.where: fly.io secrets for server-side values; local.properties (gitignored) or CI secrets for build-time values
secretsPolicy.rationale: Client IDs are public by design and may live in the repo. Secrets and private keys may not, and the repo has a pre-bash hook that scans for this.
